note: Adapted from the species description of Aderitotermes cavator in Sands (1972), originally in English: the species lacks soldiers and only the alate and the worker are described; measurement-table headers, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and figures damaged by OCR in the measurement tables are omitted; mandibular and cephalic pilosity characters covered by the generic diagnosis are not repeated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Of the two described species, this is the more specialized; the morphology of the third known species is intermediate between this species and the type species of the genus, A. fossor. It is characterized by the relatively long apical teeth of the mandibles and by enteric valves bearing wing-like appendages.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity pale yellow, very sparse. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26–0.28, Pcl/Ri 2.38–2.44. Apical teeth of the mandibles relatively long, La/Li 0.64–0.79, Ra/Ri 0.88–1.00. Fore tibia hardly inflated, T1/Tw 5.08–5.31. The enteric valve seating is connected to the second hindgut pouch by a very distinct neck of moderate length; all the enteric valve cushions protrude through the valve opening as flattened wing-like lobes, reticulate or scale-like on the surface, the posterior margin of each scale fringed with minute spines and one or two small spines; the membranous wall of the valve bears fleshy processes both between and outside the cushions, and the posterior margin of each lobe is fringed with very numerous minute spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli, the dark area sometimes extending as striae tapering towards the fontanelle; fontanelle circular or very briefly elliptical, flat or slightly concave, smaller than the ocellus, yellowish white to yellowish brown, distinct; median spot circular, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, dark brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal marking a flat brown crescent; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum brown; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae yellow, tarsi paler. Abdominal tergites dark brown, dorsolateral spiracles paler, sternites brown with the middle yellow, ventrolateral spiracles pale brown; cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule usually slightly undulate and unevenly rounded, evenly rounded in some specimens; ocelli rather large, separated from the compound eye by half or more of their own least diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.21–0.27, Pcl/Ra 1.82–2.45, posterior margin arcuate or evenly rounded, median suture present, sometimes weak. Composite ratio of mandibular and notal measurements L1/M.N 1.26–1.52.
